title: Frozen no-skill anchors make reciprocal metric-skill coevolution observationally indistinguishable from one-way metric-to-skill coupling
dead_end_scope: The standalone identifiability claim that the released Double Ratchet implementation leaves reciprocal metric-skill coupling observationally ambiguous even though the first-party update graph explicitly omits any skill-output-to-metric-data edge.

counter_explanation.statement: Reciprocal coupling is not latent in the released Double Ratchet object. The first-party implementation constructs dev_items, locked, and train once before alternating phases and later metric phases reuse those same objects, while skill phases consume the current metric through make_expr_grader. Because skill-phase outputs are not inputs to the metric update operator, the released causal graph is directly one-way rather than observationally ambiguous.
counter_explanation.opposite_prediction: For the released implementation, changing skill state or skill-phase outputs while holding the frozen metric-phase dev_items/train objects and metric random/model inputs fixed cannot alter a later metric update through a reciprocal data path, because no such input edge exists. Any measured metric change must flow through some other explicitly introduced state or instrumentation change.
counter_explanation.opposite_principle: Causal reciprocity is a structural property of update operators, not an identifiability problem when the implementation exposes the dependency graph. A missing reciprocal edge becomes scientifically interesting only through a downstream consequence that survives generic distribution-shift, stale-supervisor, or alternating-optimization reductions.
counter_explanation.opposite_search_seed: Search for self-evolving systems where actor updates materially shift the error/data distribution seen by a supervisor or evaluator, and test whether a frozen or one-way evaluator incurs held-out selection/regret consequences that cannot be explained by a same-information covariate-shift or online-adaptation baseline. Do not claim novelty from merely observing that one update operator omits the other component's outputs.
counter_explanation.scope: Double Ratchet first-party repository commit 0f14e910d361196422d9b938f45280919952d4fd, especially evalratchet/coevolve.py::_prepare, run_coevolution, run_adaptive_coevolution, make_real_skill_loop, and evalratchet/evolve.py::evolve_metric_expr.
counter_explanation.structural_witness: run_coevolution/run_adaptive_coevolution call _prepare once before all alternating phases. _prepare materializes dev_items, locked, and train from frozen no-skill solver outputs. Every later metric phase passes those same objects to evolve_metric_expr. Skill phases instead receive state.metric_expr through make_expr_grader, and their outputs are returned only as phase reports/progress summaries; they are not inserted into dev_items or train for the next metric phase.
alternative_explanations_ruled_out: Reciprocal data refresh through skill reports: phase reports update logging/progress summaries but are not assigned into dev_items or train used by evolve_metric_expr.
Hidden eval_locked feedback: eval_locked is report-only for the metric loop and does not create the missing skill-output-to-metric-data edge.

Warm skill-bank coupling: the skill bank persists across skill phases, but persistence changes the actor side only; the metric training examples remain the frozen no-skill objects prepared before alternation.
counter_explanation.reopen_condition: Reopen only with a preregistered downstream consequence of the missing reciprocal edge, such as held-out evaluator selection/regret under actor-induced distribution shift, and require the effect to survive a same-information generic distribution-shift/online-adaptation baseline and a matched compute budget.

scientific_interpretation.safe_claim: The released Double Ratchet implementation has directly observable one-way metric-to-skill coupling at the data-update level. Treating that structural fact itself as an identifiability problem is a dead end; the scientifically meaningful follow-up is whether such one-way coupling causes a nontrivial consequence beyond generic distribution shift.
do_not_say: Double Ratchet is not a useful system
all co-evolution must refresh both components on each other's raw outputs
scientific_interpretation.new_problem_seed: When actor updates change the distribution of errors seen in deployment, does a supervisor trained on frozen pre-update outputs become systematically stale in a way that changes later update decisions beyond what a generic same-information distribution-shift adapter can explain?

opposite_search_asset_evidence.title: Double Ratchet first-party metric/skill co-evolution implementation
empirical_facts: run_coevolution calls _prepare once before alternating phases, and later metric phases reuse the same dev_items, locked, and train objects created from frozen no-skill outputs.

Skill phases consume the current metric through make_expr_grader and update the warm skill bank, but their outputs are not inserted into the metric-phase dev_items or train objects used by subsequent evolve_metric_expr calls.
The released adaptive controller gates on metric maturity and metric-graded skill train progress while eval_locked remains report-only for the metric side.
